\chapter{Complexity — Virtual Input}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.VirtualInput}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Virtual host buffer index]
\lean{Turing.vhostBuffer}
\label{Turing.vhostBuffer}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$, let the virtual host’s buffer tape be the first of its $m+1$
work tapes, indexed by $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual host bank indices]
\lean{Turing.vhostBank}
\label{Turing.vhostBank}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$, the virtual host’s bank tapes are the remaining $m$ work
tapes: bank tape $i$, for $0 \le i < m$, has index $i+1$ among the $m+1$ work tapes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual host configuration]
\lean{Turing.vhostCfg}
\label{Turing.vhostCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
Let $c$ be a configuration of an $m$-work-tape machine on input $y$, with Boolean
symbols and states in $S$. Given a Boolean tag $b$, a new input-head position $p$ for
input $x$, and a Boolean list $\mathrm{pre}$, form a configuration with $m+1$ work tapes
and states in $S\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$: its state is $c$’s state paired
with $b$, its input-head position is $p$, its first work tape is the buffer tape
initialized from $y$, and its remaining work tapes and head positions are those of $c$.
The head position on the first tape is $c$’s input-head index minus one, and the output
is $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $c$’s output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual host transition machine]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.virtualMove, Turing.FinTM.virtualNextTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.vhostBank, Turing.vhostBuffer}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $m$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and states in
$S$. The constructed machine has $m+1$ work tapes and states in
$S\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and starts in $(q_0,\mathrm{true})$. On a
transition, it reads the symbol on the first work tape as the simulated input symbol and
reads the remaining tapes as $M$’s work tapes; it uses $M$’s transition and the current
tag to determine the input-head movement and the next tag. It leaves the first tape
unwritten, applies the resulting movement to each of the remaining tapes, and preserves
the simulated output and successor state, pairing that state with the next tag when
there is a successor.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Virtual host cap index]
\lean{Turing.vhostCap}
\label{Turing.vhostCap}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$, the virtual host’s cap tape is the last of its $m+2$ work
tapes, indexed by $m+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Silent virtual host machine]
\lean{Turing.vhostSilentTM}
\label{Turing.vhostSilentTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.embedSilentTM, Turing.vhostCap, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $m$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and states in
$S$. The silent virtual host machine is obtained by applying the silent-tape embedding
to the virtual host machine built from $M$, using the last tape as the cap tape.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Silent virtual-host configuration]
\lean{Turing.vhostSilentCfg}
\label{Turing.vhostSilentCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.embedSilentCfg, Turing.vhostCap, Turing.vhostCfg}
Let $m$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a type of states, and let $x,y$ be finite
Boolean strings. For a configuration $c$ with $m$ work tapes on input $y$, a Boolean
$b$, an input-head position $p$ for $x$, and Boolean strings $\mathrm{capPre}$ and
$\mathrm{out}_0$, define the silent virtual-host configuration by applying the
silent-configuration embedding to the virtual-host configuration of $c$ with tag $b$,
position $p$, and empty output, using the designated cap tape, cap prefix
$\mathrm{capPre}$, and output prefix $\mathrm{out}_0$, with the added tape blank
everywhere and its head at position zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-Step Virtual Simulation]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_step}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.virtualMove, Turing.FinTM.virtualMove_correct, Turing.FinTM.virtualNextTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.vhostBank, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with state set $S$, and let
$c$ be a configuration on a Boolean input word $y$. If $b$ satisfies the boundary
condition for $c$'s input-head position, then for every Boolean input word $x$, every
virtual input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, and every Boolean list
$\mathrm{pre}$, there is a Boolean tag $b'$ satisfying the boundary condition for the
input-head position after one step of $M$, such that one step of the virtual simulation
from the configuration built from $c,b,p,\mathrm{pre}$ equals the configuration built
from the one-step successor of $c$, tag $b'$, the same $p$, and the same $\mathrm{pre}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation for Any Number of Steps]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with state set $S$, and let
$c$ be a configuration on a Boolean input word $y$. If $b$ satisfies the boundary
condition for $c$'s input-head position, then for every Boolean input word $x$, every
virtual input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, every Boolean list
$\mathrm{pre}$, and every $t\in\mathbb N$, there is a Boolean tag $b'$ satisfying the
boundary condition for the input-head position reached by $M$ after $t$ steps, such that
the virtual simulation after $t$ steps is exactly the configuration built from that
reached configuration, tag $b'$, the same position $p$, and the same list
$\mathrm{pre}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Visited cells on embedded work tapes]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_bank}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_bank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.vhostBank, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a Boolean-input multi-tape Turing machine with $m$ work tapes, and let $c$ be
a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose the Boolean tag $b$ marks the boundary of
the input-head position of $c$: at position $0$ it is false, and at position $|y|+1$ it
is true. For any Boolean word $x$, position $p$ on its input tape, output prefix, time
$t$, and work-tape index $i<m$, the cells visited by the head on bank tape $i$ of the
virtual-host machine from the corresponding virtual-host configuration through time $t$
are exactly the cells visited by work-tape head $i$ of $M$ from $c$ through time $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Visited cells of the virtual input head]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_buffer}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_buffer}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a Boolean-input multi-tape Turing machine with $m$ work tapes, and let $c$ be
a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose the Boolean tag $b$ marks the boundary of
the input-head position of $c$: at position $0$ it is false, and at position $|y|+1$ it
is true. For any Boolean word $x$, input-head position $p$ among its $|x|+2$ positions,
output prefix, and time $t$, the cells visited by the virtual-host machine's buffer-tape
head through time $t$ are exactly the integers obtained by subtracting $1$ from the
input-head position of $M$ at each time $u=0,1,\ldots,t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the Virtual Buffer Head]
\lean{Turing.vhostCfg_buffer_head_mem}
\label{Turing.vhostCfg_buffer_head_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a Turing machine with $m$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet and state set
$S$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a Boolean input word $y$. If the Boolean
tag $b$ correctly marks the boundary of the input head of $c$, then for every Boolean
input word $x$, every virtual input-head position $p$ for a word of length $|x|$, every
Boolean list $\mathrm{pre}$, and every $t\in\mathbb N$, the head on the added buffer
tape in the virtual simulation started from the configuration built from
$c,b,p,\mathrm{pre}$ lies between $-1$ and $|y|$, inclusive, after $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space Bound for the Virtual Simulation]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_spaceUsed_le}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_spaceUsed_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape, Turing.vhostBank, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostCfg_buffer_head_mem, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_bank}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with state set $S$, and let
$c$ be a configuration on a Boolean input word $y$. If $b$ satisfies the boundary
condition for $c$'s input-head position, then for every Boolean input word $x$, every
virtual input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, every Boolean list
$\mathrm{pre}$, and every $t\in\mathbb N$, the total space used by the virtual
simulation from the configuration built from $c,b,p,\mathrm{pre}$ through step $t$ is at
most the space used by $M$ from $c$ through step $t$, plus $|y|+2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Emitting Transition That Halts]
\lean{Turing.vhostEmitTM_emitting_halt}
\label{Turing.vhostEmitTM_emitting_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an $m$-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with state set $S$, and let
$c$ be a configuration on a Boolean input word $y$. Suppose $c$ is in state $q$, the
Boolean tag $b$ satisfies the boundary condition for its input-head position, and the
transition of $M$ from $q$ on the symbols currently read halts while emitting the bit
$a$. For any Boolean input word $x$, any virtual input-head position $p$ among the
$|x|+2$ positions, and any Boolean list $\mathrm{pre}$, one step of the virtual
simulation from the configuration built from $c,b,p,\mathrm{pre}$ has no state and has
output $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by the output of $c$ and then $a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Layout of the silent-simulation tapes]
\lean{Turing.vhostSilent_layout}
\label{Turing.vhostSilent_layout}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.vhostCap}
\difficulty{4}
For a natural number $m$ and any tape index $j\in\{0,\ldots,m+1\}$, $j$ lies in the
image of the standard embedding of the first $m+1$ tape indices into these $m+2$ indices
if and only if $j<m+1$. It lies outside that image if and only if $j$ is the final index
$m+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run correspondence for the silent simulation]
\lean{Turing.vhostSilentTM_runFrom}
\label{Turing.vhostSilentTM_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.embedSilentTM_runFrom, Turing.vhostCap, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom, Turing.vhostSilentCfg, Turing.vhostSilentTM, Turing.vhostSilent_layout}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $m$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, and let
$c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose
$b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ satisfies: if the input-head position of $c$ is
$0$, then $b=\mathrm{false}$, and if that position is $|y|+1$, then $b=\mathrm{true}$.
For any Boolean word $x$, any input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, any
Boolean lists $u$ and $v$, and any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a Boolean tag $b'$
satisfying the same boundary conditions for the input-head position of the configuration
reached from $c$ after $t$ steps, such that running the silent simulation for $t$ steps
from the corresponding encoded configuration gives exactly the encoded configuration of
that $t$-step run, with tag $b'$ and the same $p,u,v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound for the silent simulation]
\lean{Turing.vhostSilentTM_spaceUsed_le}
\label{Turing.vhostSilentTM_spaceUsed_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape, Turing.embedSilentTM_spaceUsedByTape_cap, Turing.embedSilentTM_visitedByTapeHead, Turing.vhostCap, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom, Turing.vhostEmitTM_spaceUsed_le, Turing.vhostSilentCfg, Turing.vhostSilentTM, Turing.vhostSilent_layout}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a Boolean-symbol Turing machine with $m$ work tapes, and let $c$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Let $b$ be a Boolean tag such that the input-head
position of $c$ is $0$ only if $b$ is false, and is $|y|+1$ only if $b$ is true. For any
Boolean word $x$, any input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ positions, any Boolean
lists $u$ and $v$, and any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the total number of distinct cells visited
by the work-tape heads of the silent simulation of $M$ from the configuration built from
$c,b,p,u,v$, through time $t$, is at most the number visited by $M$ from $c$ through
time $t$, plus $|y|+2+|u\mathbin{++}(M\text{'s output after }t\text{ steps from }c)|+1$.
\end{theorem}
